moment.text: As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly. He will become the father of twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.

previous.text: God said, “No, but Sarah, your wife, will bear you a son. You shall call his name Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.

next.text: But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this set time next year.”

section.title: Promise of Isaac and Ishmael's blessing

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

aliases: Abraham the father of many nations
canon.name: Abram
canon.note: Son of Terah from Ur, called to Canaan and renamed Abraham; the same patriarch as Galatians' Abraham, so both entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Abram / Abraham

quotes.quote: Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years
Lot went with him.

stages.text: Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.

canon.name: Sarai/Sarah, wife of Abraham
canon.note: Wife of Abram, barren until she bears Isaac in old age and renamed Sarah; the same woman is cited in Romans, Hebrews and 1 Peter as Abraham's wife.

stages.label: Sarai / Sarah

quotes.quote: I know that you are a beautiful woman to look at.
Sarai was barren. She had no child.
her name shall be Sarah.
Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age.

stages.text: Sarah: a woman of about sixty to ninety, slender and upright, with dark skin of the Ancient Near East. Her face is fine-boned and dignified, with a calm, serious gaze. Her hair is dark, bound under a plain linen headcloth, with a few grey strands showing at the temples. Her signature outfit is a long undyed wool tunic in ochre with a dark brown woollen shawl over the shoulders. She carries no props.

aliases: the hill country of the Amorites
canon.name: Canaan
canon.note: The promised land of Israel as a whole, the land Yahweh gives to Abram's descendants, referred to in Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges and Hebrews alike; all six entries describe this same land.

stages.label: Canaan, the promised land

quotes.quote: Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
Behold, Yahweh your God has set the land before you.
to the Western Sea
the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession
seven nations greater and mightier than you

stages.text: Canaan: a fertile hill country between the Jordan river and the Western Sea, with terraced slopes, olive groves, vineyards heavy with grapes, wheat fields in the valleys, and wells beside walled mud-brick and stone towns on the hilltops. Scattered oaks and terebinths mark old sacred places, and herders' pastures roll toward the distant coast.

fields.primarySubject: Veiled radiance with a fire-like heart filling the upper sky above an unoccupied seat-like space; Abram stands below, gazing upward.
fields.action: Abram stands with his face lifted toward the radiance while the dense cloud slowly drifts across the sky; the radiance pulses faintly without moving downward.
fields.setting: Open wild land near a mud-brick tent encampment, with a dry well and a stone altar at the edge of the grazing ground.
fields.secondaryElements: A water skin and shepherd's staff resting near the tents; dust lifting faintly from the dry ground; the stone altar at the field's edge.
fields.mood: Reverent, quiet and expectant, with a sense of solemn promise held in stillness.
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon, sun low over the hills with dusk gathering at the far edge of the land.
fields.composition: Wide landscape viewed from a low angle, with the radiance dominating the upper third and Abram small in the lower centre against the open ground.

conditions.place: Open wild land near a mud-brick tent encampment, with a dry well and a stone altar at the edge of the grazing ground.
conditions.timeOfDay: Late afternoon in a single outdoor scene, sun low over the hills, with dusk gathering at the far edge of the land.
conditions.weather: Clear, still air with a dense slow-moving cloud bank high overhead and dust lifting faintly from the dry ground.
conditions.light: Warm evening sun, with a brilliant white-gold radiance without source, veiled by cloud and glowing with a fire-like heart, filling the upper sky.
conditions.clothing: Simple undyed wool wraps, linen tunics and sandals; a water skin and a shepherd's staff near the tents.

moment.text: Yahweh appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.

section.title: The three visitors and Sarah's laughter

canon.name: The three visitors at Mamre and the two angels at Sodom
canon.note: The three men who visit Abraham and the two angels who rescue Lot in Genesis, treated as one group of visitors; not the two white-robed angels at the empty tomb in John.

stages.label: The visitors (typical member)

quotes.quote: The two angels came to Sodom at evening. Lot sat in the gate of Sodom.

stages.text: The visitors: men of mature adult age, neither young nor old; lean and sturdy build; skin weathered brown by desert sun; short dark beard and hair cropped close to the head; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen wrap over a short wool tunic in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a plain wooden staff, the only prop.

Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years
Lot went with him.

Sarai was barren. She had no child.

canon.name: Mamre (the oaks of Mamre)
canon.note: The oak grove near Hebron where Abraham dwells, receives the three visitors and buries Sarah; distinct from the town of Hebron itself, though the aliases overlap.

stages.label: The oaks of Mamre

quotes.quote: Abram moved his tent, and came and lived by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built an altar there to Yahweh.
the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, the cave which was in it, and all the trees
Yahweh appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.

stages.text: Mamre: a rolling upland grove near Hebron, in a dry hill country of limestone ridges and scrub. Great old terebinth and oak trees stand in a broad clearing, their wide trunks and grey-green canopies giving shade. Among them lie a level field with a cave at its edge, a spring or well nearby, and herders' tent-camps of dark goat-hair cloth. Low stone walls mark the field's bounds; no buildings beyond tents and altars of piled stone.

fields.primarySubject: Veiled white-gold radiance with a fire-like glow at its heart, seen at the grove's edge beside the oaks; Abram seated in the tent door, gazing toward it.
fields.action: Abram sits still in the tent door, body upright and attentive, turned toward the radiance at the grove's edge; the veiled cloud of light stays at rest beside the oaks.
fields.setting: Oak grove at Mamre beside a tent door of woven goat hair, with dry wild land and distant mud-brick town edges; an empty stone-ringed well nearby.
fields.secondaryElements: A clay water jar and wooden staff placed near the tent door; oak leaves overhead; faint dust hanging over the dry ground.
fields.mood: Still, reverent expectancy in the heat of the day, with quiet awe at the edge of the grove.
fields.timeOfDay: Midday heat, bright and still, with long shadows softening toward late afternoon.
fields.composition: Medium-wide view from the tent interior looking out; Abram in the doorway at left, oaks across the middle, radiance at the grove's edge at right.

conditions.place: Oak grove at Mamre beside a tent door of woven goat hair, with a dry wild land and distant mud-brick town edges; an empty stone-ringed well nearby.
conditions.timeOfDay: Midday heat, bright and still, with long shadows softening toward late afternoon.
conditions.weather: Clear, hot and windless air, dust hanging faintly over the dry ground.
conditions.light: Strong midday sun through oak leaves; a veiled brilliant white-gold radiance with a fire-like glow at the heart of a slowly moving cloud, shown only at the grove's edge.
conditions.clothing: Simple undyed wool and linen wraps and tunics, sandals, a clay water jar and a wooden staff placed near the tent door.

moment.text: He judged Israel twenty years in the days of the Philistines.

previous.text: But God split the hollow place that is in Lehi, and water came out of it. When he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived. Therefore its name was called En Hakkore, which is in Lehi, to this day.

section.title: Foxes, the men of Judah, and the jawbone

canon.name: Samson
canon.note: Nazirite judge of Dan whose exploits against the Philistines include the riddle, the foxes, the jawbone, and the temple of Dagon.

stages.label: Samson

quotes.quote: No razor shall come on his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb.
The woman bore a son and named him Samson. The child grew, and Yahweh blessed him.
No razor has ever come on my head; for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb.

stages.text: Samson: a strong man in his prime, roughly thirty years old, broad-shouldered and powerfully muscled with a lean, weathered frame; sun-browned olive skin; long, uncut hair falling past his shoulders, dark brown, and a full untrimmed beard; a grave, dignified face with a strong nose and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a woven undyed linen tunic in ochre with a plain brown wool cloak. Signature prop: none he carries; his only sign is the unshorn hair.

canon.name: Philistines
canon.note: The oppressors of Israel and lords of the Philistines in Samson's story; a foreign people, not an Israelite tribe.

stages.label: Philistines (typical warrior of the lords' armies)

quotes.quote: the five lords of the Philistines
thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen

stages.text: Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.

canon.name: Judah (tribe)
canon.note: The tribe of Judah in Judges, leading the attacks on Canaanite cities; the same tribal group as the southern kingdom addressed in Hosea, so one cluster is applied to both entries.

stages.label: Judah (tribe)

quotes.quote: Judah shall go up. Behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.
Yahweh was with Judah, and drove out the inhabitants of the hill country

stages.text: Judah: a tribe of Israel's highland men, typically adult, seasoned and sun-browned, of lean and sturdy build, with olive to tan skin, short dark hair and close-cut beards. Faces are weathered and resolute. Signature dress: undyed or earth-brown woven wool tunic belted with cord, over it a dark brown cloak of woven goat hair, with a leather sling or short sword at the belt. Shared props: round shields of wood and hide, slung leather bags for stones.

canon.name: Timnah (Philistine town)
canon.note: Philistine town where Samson takes a wife, kills a lion and sets his riddle; distinct from the Judahite Timnah of Genesis.

stages.label: Timnah, Philistine town

quotes.quote: Samson went down to Timnah, and saw a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.
came to the vineyards of Timnah; and behold, a young lion roared at him.

stages.text: Timnah: a walled Philistine town on a low ridge of the Shephelah, with mud-brick and stone houses, flat roofs and a gate of heavy timber. Terraced vineyards of trained vines and olive trees climb the slopes beyond the town, with rough stone walls between them and scrub and rocky hollows in the lower ground.

canon.name: cave in Etam's rock
canon.note: Cave where Samson hides from the men of Judah.

stages.label: Cave in Etam's rock

quotes.quote: he went down and lived in the cave in Etam’s rock.
went down to the cave in Etam’s rock

stages.text: Cave in Etam's rock: a rugged limestone outcrop in the hill country of Judah, its grey stone weathered and broken into ledges. The cave mouth is a low, irregular opening in the cliff face, shaded by scrub oak, terebinth and wild thorn growing from cracks in the rock. Loose stones and dry grass lie at the foot of the escarpment, with the wider hills rising in terraces beyond.

canon.name: Lehi
canon.note: Place where Samson kills a thousand men with a jawbone and drinks from a spring.

stages.label: Lehi

quotes.quote: the Philistines went up, encamped in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.
God split the hollow place that is in Lehi, and water came out of it.

stages.text: Lehi: a rough, sunlit hill country of Judah, with low ridges of pale limestone, scattered scrub, terebinth and wild grass in the dry hollows. A broad flat clearing of packed earth lies among the rocks, where a cleft in the stone opens into a hollow place from which a cool spring rises.

fields.primarySubject: Samson, a lone judge standing still in the hill country.
fields.action: He stands at rest, looking out over the land, a quiet moment of rule held across the years of Philistine dominion.
fields.setting: Rocky ridges and olive groves of Philistine-controlled hill country near Timnah, with dry wheat fields spreading below.
fields.secondaryElements: Distant low hills and a few scattered stones; no other figures in the frame, only the empty land under evening sky.
fields.mood: Solemn, weary and steadfast, with a sense of endurance under foreign rule.
fields.composition: Wide view from a low ridge, Samson placed small in the lower third against the open land and darkening sky.

conditions.weather: Clear, dry, warm and still with no rain
conditions.light: Low amber sun fading to blue dusk

moment.text: Doesn’t Hezekiah persuade you to give you over to die by famine and by thirst, saying, ‘Yahweh our God will deliver us out of the hand of the king of Assyria’?

previous.text: Sennacherib king of Assyria says, “In whom do you trust, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?

next.text: Hasn’t the same Hezekiah taken away his high places and his altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You shall worship before one altar, and you shall burn incense on it’?

aliases: king of Judah son of Ahaz
canon.name: Hezekiah
canon.note: Reforming king of Judah son of Ahaz who receives Isaiah.

stages.label: Hezekiah, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.
And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into Yahweh’s house.

stages.text: Hezekiah: a man in his late twenties to forties, lean and upright, of Israelite stock. Olive-brown skin, close-trimmed dark beard, dark hair pinned under a royal fillet. Grave, weathered face. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep-blue royal court robe with a woven gold border. Signature prop: a plain wooden royal staff.

canon.name: Sennacherib
canon.note: King of Assyria who besieges Jerusalem and is killed by his sons.

stages.label: Sennacherib, king of Assyria

quotes.quote: Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went home, and lived at Nineveh.

stages.text: Sennacherib: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and commanding; olive-brown skin; a full, carefully curled dark beard and short-cropped hair beneath a tall, conical royal crown banded with gold; a dark, strong face with heavy brows and a steady, severe gaze. He wears a long embroidered court robe of crimson and gold over a fringed tunic, with a deep-blue royal cloak, and bears a royal staff and an ornate gold-hilted sword at his belt.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
canon.name: Jerusalem
canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Hezekiah, king of Judah, standing on the city wall above the gate.
fields.action: Hezekiah addresses the people of Jerusalem gathered below, one arm lifted toward the city, urging them to trust in their God for deliverance.
fields.setting: The wall and gate of Jerusalem on its hills, with the Assyrian siege camp visible in the distance beyond the walls.
fields.secondaryElements: Jerusalem's people in tunics and cloaks gather below the wall, some looking up at the king; dust hangs in the air and long shadows fall from the wall.
fields.mood: Tense, sorrowful and resolute, with a quiet dignity under threat.
fields.composition: Low-angle view from below the wall, with Hezekiah high and central against the sky and the crowd filling the lower foreground.

conditions.place: Jerusalem's city wall and gate, with the Assyrian camp beyond
conditions.weather: Dry, hazy summer heat with dust in the air
conditions.light: Harsh bright sunlight with long shadows at the edges, warm and clear
conditions.clothing: Tunics and cloaks for Jerusalem's people; royal robes for Hezekiah; no emblems or inscriptions shown

moment.text: for the king’s word is supreme. Who can say to him, “What are you doing?”

canon.name: Under the sun
canon.note: The general setting of earthly human activity described throughout; not a single place.

stages.label: Under the sun

quotes.quote: under the sun
all that is done under the sky
If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth

stages.text: Under the sun: a wide, sun-bleached Levantine earth of dry hill country and terraced fields, with stone walls, olive and terebinth trees, winding river beds, and distant walled cities of pale limestone beneath an open sky.

fields.primarySubject: A courtier standing still before the columned palace gate, awaiting or hearing the king's word, not questioning it.
fields.action: The king's command is pronounced; no one answers or challenges it, and the courtier holds a respectful, attentive stillness.
fields.setting: An open courtyard before a Persian-style palace with stone walls and a columned gate, dusty ground.
fields.secondaryElements: Guards in period armor stand at the gate; courtiers in embroidered court robes remain at a distance; the palace doorway is shaded behind the columns.
fields.mood: Solemn, restrained and weighty, with an undercurrent of unspoken submission.
fields.composition: Wide frame from the courtyard looking toward the columned gate, the courtier small in the middle ground with the palace rising behind.

conditions.place: Open courtyard before a Persian-style palace, with stone walls, columned gate and dusty ground
conditions.light: Harsh direct sunlight casting short shadows
conditions.clothing: Tunics and cloaks of linen and wool, court robes with embroidered hems, period armor for guards

moment.text: When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, “Give us bread, for why should we die in your presence? For our money fails.”

previous.text: Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.

next.text: Joseph said, “Give me your livestock; and I will give you food for your livestock, if your money is gone.”

canon.name: Joseph son of Jacob (the dreamer)
canon.note: Favorite son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into Egypt and later ruler under Pharaoh; the Genesis figure, also named in Judges as the house of Joseph's ancestor, Acts and Hebrews as the patriarch; not the husband of Mary.

stages.label: Joseph, son of Jacob

quotes.quote: Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers.
Joseph was well-built and handsome.
he made him a tunic of many colors.
arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Joseph lived one hundred ten years.

stages.text: Joseph: a young man of about seventeen in youth, rising to a mature man of thirty and later an elder of one hundred ten; well-built and handsome, lean and strong from shepherding, with warm brown skin, dark hair cut short, a smooth-shaven face in Egyptian style, dark eyes and a steady, gentle expression. Signature outfit: a long tunic of many colours in Canaanite style, bright reds, blues and yellows; in Egypt, robes of white or cream fine linen. Signature props: a gold chain at the neck and Pharaoh's signet ring on the hand.

canon.name: Pharaoh of Joseph
canon.note: Egyptian king of Joseph's era who dreams of cattle and grain and elevates Joseph; the king who knew Joseph, distinct from the Exodus oppressor.

stages.label: Pharaoh of Joseph

quotes.quote: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

stages.text: Pharaoh of Joseph: man in his fifties; broad, dignified build; deep bronze skin; close-cropped dark hair under a tall blue and gold royal headcloth with a cobra emblem; neatly trimmed beard, ceremonial false beard; calm, grave face. Signature outfit: white pleated linen kilt and shendyt with a broad golden collar in blue and gold. Props: gold signet ring, gold chain, crook and flail of office.

canon.name: Egypt
canon.note: The land of Egypt where patriarchs sojourn, Israel is enslaved and plagues fall; recurs in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Psalms, Ezekiel, Hosea, Micah and Hebrews as the same land.

stages.label: Egypt

quotes.quote: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen
But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them
for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.

stages.text: Egypt: a long green valley of the Nile flanked by pale desert; broad river channels, canals and reed marsh; fertile black earth fields of barley and flax; date palms and sycamores; mud-brick and limestone cities with tall temple pylons, obelisks and fortified walls; the Delta with its towns of Goshen and Zoan.

fields.primarySubject: Joseph standing at the granary doorway, facing the approaching crowd of Egyptian petitioners.
fields.action: The Egyptian people come up to Joseph with empty hands held out, asking for bread, while Joseph stands still and attentive at the doorway.
fields.setting: Egypt's granaries beside the Nile, with mud-brick storehouses and dry fields stretching to the horizon.
fields.secondaryElements: Empty clay jars and grain sacks on the ground; a few palm trees casting shadows; the crowd of Egyptian men, women and children, some with bowed heads.
fields.mood: Anxious, reverent and quietly dignified, carrying the weight of famine.
fields.timeOfDay: Midday through afternoon, the sun high and hot over a long famine season.
fields.composition: Wide view from the granary threshold, Joseph in the foreground at the doorway, the crowd approaching across the open ground in the middle distance.

conditions.place: Egypt's granaries and storehouses beside the Nile, with dry fields and mud-brick buildings stretching to the horizon
conditions.timeOfDay: Midday through afternoon, the sun high and hot over a long famine season
conditions.weather: Dry, windless heat under a clear pale sky, dust hanging in the air
conditions.light: Harsh golden sunlight with deep shadows cast by storehouse walls and palm trees
conditions.clothing: Simple linen wraps and tunics, sandals, headcloths against the sun; clay jars and grain sacks as props

moment.text: Afterward they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

previous.text: After these things, he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

next.text: When he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’

section.title: Paul's sermon at Antioch of Pisidia

canon.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
canon.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

canon.name: Barnabas
canon.note: Levite of Cyprus, also called Joses, who travels with Paul.

stages.label: Barnabas

quotes.quote: a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race

stages.text: Barnabas: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and steady, with a weathered olive-brown skin from sea and road. Short dark hair going grey at the temples, and a neatly trimmed dark beard. Calm, warm eyes and a broad, open face. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long cream-brown wool cloak. Carries a worn leather travelling satchel and a wooden staff.

canon.name: Crowd in Acts
canon.note: The crowd gathering in Jerusalem, Ephesus, Lystra and elsewhere to hear, mock or riot in Acts.

stages.label: Crowd in Acts

quotes.quote: the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

stages.text: Crowd in Acts: a typical member is an adult of about twenty to fifty years, lean and sun-browned from working outdoors, with dark brown or black hair worn short or tied back and beards kept short on men. Skin olive to tawny, faces weathered and serious. Clothing: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or earth-brown, a dark wool cloak in deep blue or grey, sandals. Carries no props of his own.

canon.name: Antioch of Pisidia
canon.note: City in Pisidia (Asia Minor) where Paul preaches in the synagogue and turns to the Gentiles; distinct from Antioch of Syria by region.

stages.label: Antioch of Pisidia

quotes.quote: they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia
They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down.

stages.text: Antioch of Pisidia: a Roman colonial city on a high plateau of Pisidia in Asia Minor, ringed by rugged limestone mountains capped with snow. Pale stone city walls and wide paved streets lined with colonnades of white marble, Roman civic buildings with tiled roofs, and a stone synagogue of plain dressed masonry near the centre. Olive groves, cypress and oleander grow on the slopes; dry grass and scrub cover the plateau beyond.

fields.primarySubject: Saul of Tarsus (Paul), standing and addressing the congregation with one hand raised.
fields.action: He speaks the recounting of Israel's history at the moment the people's request for a king is named and Saul son of Kish is given to them.
fields.setting: Interior of a stone synagogue in Antioch of Pisidia, with wooden benches, high windows and an open doorway onto a paved street.
fields.secondaryElements: The seated crowd in prayer shawls on wooden benches listens, some turning toward the speaker; a lamp hangs near the wall; sunlight falls through the doorway onto the stone floor.
fields.mood: Solemn, attentive and reverent, with a sense of weighty history.
fields.timeOfDay: Sabbath afternoon, with sun high and beginning to lower.
fields.composition: Medium-wide view from the back of the synagogue, Saul centered near the front, the crowd arranged on benches in the foreground and the open doorway visible behind.

conditions.place: Synagogue in a Roman colonial city, Antioch of Pisidia, with stone walls, wooden benches and an open doorway onto a paved street
conditions.timeOfDay: Sabbath afternoon, sun high then lowering
conditions.weather: Clear, dry Anatolian sky with light breeze
conditions.light: Warm golden daylight streaming through high windows and doorway, soft shadows on stone
conditions.clothing: Linen tunics, woolen cloaks and prayer shawls in earth tones; Roman soldiers in red-trimmed military dress at the edge of the street

moment.text: The king of Egypt was told that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed toward the people, and they said, “What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?”

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
canon.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
canon.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: Pharaoh (king of Egypt who did not know Joseph)
canon.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus (oppressor of Israel)
canon.note: The unnamed king of Egypt in Exodus who enslaves Israel, hardens his heart against Moses and suffers the plagues; the same king recalled in Deuteronomy and cited in Romans 9:17 as the one raised up to show God's power.

stages.label: Pharaoh of the Exodus

quotes.quote: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them
Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them

stages.text: Pharaoh of the Exodus: man in his fifties, tall and broad-shouldered, dark brown skin; close-cropped hair under a blue-and-gold nemes headcloth, and a short trimmed false beard of the royal style; calm, hard features with heavy-lidded eyes and a firm mouth. Signature outfit: white linen kilt with a pleated gold-edged apron, broad gold collar, and red-and-gold royal sash. Signature props: gold crook and flail of royal office, carried alone.

canon.name: the Egyptians
canon.note: The Egyptian people, officers and magicians in Exodus who oppress Israel and suffer the plagues; distinguished from the Egyptian magicians of Genesis and from the Chaldeans of Babylon.

stages.label: the Egyptians

quotes.quote: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.

stages.text: the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt or wrap-tunic with a linen cloak in ochre and blue. Signature props: none carried alone; officers may bear a staff of office.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

canon.name: Red Sea
canon.note: The sea in Exodus that parts for Israel and closes over Pharaoh's army; distinct from the other seas by its setting in the exodus narrative.

stages.label: Red Sea

quotes.quote: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night
the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

stages.text: Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.

canon.name: The wilderness (Exodus route)
canon.note: The desert stretches Israel travels from Egypt through Shur, Sin and Marah, with manna, quail and water miracles; the same wilderness as the Psalms and Amos references.

stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.

fields.mood: Shock, unease and reluctant regret settling over the court
fields.timeOfDay: Late dusk, with the last evening glow entering through the doorway
fields.composition: Medium shot from the side of the hall, Pharaoh at the center on the throne, servants arranged around him, the open doorway framing the dusky sky

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

fields.primarySubject: Moses bowing low, head bent toward the earth; above the summit, radiance veiled by a slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart.
fields.action: Moses kneels and bows his head to the ground in worship; the veiled radiance hangs motionless above the summit, the cloud drifting slowly around it.
fields.setting: Rocky slopes of Horeb/Mount Sinai, barren stone and dust, with the cloud-veiled summit above and a wilderness plain far below.
fields.secondaryElements: Distant tents on the wilderness plain below; low drifting cloud around the summit; no other figures.
fields.mood: Reverent and awed, hushed stillness, humble devotion.
fields.timeOfDay: Early morning, first light rising over the wilderness.
fields.composition: Moses in the foreground lower frame, bowed; the veiled radiance and summit rising in the upper background, the plain receding below.

canon.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
canon.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

canon.name: Zion (holy hill / Mount Zion)
canon.note: The holy hill or temple mountain where Yahweh dwells and reigns, referred to as Zion, Mount Zion, or my holy mountain across psalms, joel, amos, micah, 1-peter and revelation; one hill identity, distinct from the city of Jerusalem.

stages.label: Zion, holy hill

quotes.quote: Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the north sides, the city of the great King.
As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so Yahweh surrounds his people from this time forward and forever more.
Walk about Zion, and go around her. Number its towers.

stages.text: Zion: a high rocky limestone hill rising above a ring of surrounding mountains, its slopes terraced with olive and fig trees and bordered by cedar-brown woods. Upon the summit stand the walled sanctuary courts of Yahweh's temple of pale stone and cedar, with tall gates and fortified towers along the walls of the city.

fields.primarySubject: Zion, the holy hill, as a restored place with rebuilt walls and a gate rising above the terraced slopes.
fields.action: Stone walls and a city gate stand restored on the hill, with newly set foundation stones marking the rebuilding of the cities of Judah.
fields.setting: Zion above Jerusalem, among terraced hills and olive groves, with the ruins of the old city being rebuilt around the hilltop.
fields.secondaryElements: Freshly laid stone courses, a gate of worked timber and stone, olive trees on the slopes, and soft clouds drifting over the hills; no human figures are formed in this instant.
fields.mood: Reverent hope and quiet restoration, with grief giving way to dignity.
fields.timeOfDay: Early morning, with warm golden sunrise light beginning to brighten toward full day.
fields.composition: Wide view from below the hill, with Zion centered and its walls and gate rising in the foreground, the terraced hills and olive groves receding behind.

canon.name: Solomon
canon.note: Son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel who builds the temple; the same individual across all divisions. Distinguish from the Shulammite's shepherd beloved, who is not Solomon.

stages.label: Solomon, king of Israel

quotes.quote: had Solomon ride on King David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
sat down on his throne and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother

stages.text: Solomon: man in his twenties to forties, lean and upright with a composed, dignified bearing; warm olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard; calm, thoughtful face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long deep-blue royal court robe with gold-thread borders over a white linen tunic, and a gold circlet on his head. Signature prop: a plain rod of royal authority carried alone.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion

canon.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
canon.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

fields.mood: Reverent, joyful and expectant, with communal gravity.
fields.timeOfDay: Daytime at the start of a seven-day feast.

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. stages.label: Ezekiel's temple

quotes.quote: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side.
There were made on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm trees, like those made on the walls.
He measured the court, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square. The altar was before the house.

stages.text: Ezekiel's temple: a walled sanctuary on the mountain of Jerusalem, built of pale dressed limestone with cedar panelling, its inner court paved and square, its nave carved with cherubim and palm trees between which a face of a man and a face of a young lion alternate. Gates of the outer court face east, north and south; side chambers rise in three stories. Olive and cedar trees line the courts; a river flows from beneath the threshold.

fields.primarySubject: The man clothed in linen standing in the threshold of the south gate, measuring its post with a reed.
fields.action: He holds the measuring reed against the gate post while Ezekiel stands beside him at the gate, looking on.
fields.setting: A stone gate facing south with tall posts and arches, set within an austere stone temple court beneath open sky.
fields.secondaryElements: A measuring cord and reed in the man's hands; Ezekiel in plain priestly linen beside the post; a faint radiant cloud veil at the edge of the scene.
fields.mood: Reverent and measured, with quiet attention and dignity.
fields.composition: Eye-level view from within the court, gate arch framing the measuring figure and Ezekiel, with the gate extending into depth.

conditions.place: Interior vision of a vast temple court; a stone gate facing south with tall posts and arches, set in an austere stone precinct beneath open sky.
conditions.timeOfDay: Steady daylight throughout the section, with no change in time.
conditions.weather: Clear, still air with a faint low cloud veil drifting slowly above the temple precinct.
conditions.light: Even, clear daylight across the stone, with a soft radiant glow from the cloud veil at the edges of the scene.
conditions.clothing: Priestly linen garments and a measuring cord and reed as shared props of the measuring figure.

moment.text: You shall not bow yourself down to them, nor serve them, for I, Yahweh your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children and on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me

previous.text: “You shall not make a carved image for yourself—any likeness of what is in heaven above, or what is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.

next.text: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.

section.title: The covenant at Horeb and the ten commandments

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
canon.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
canon.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

canon.name: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy
canon.note: Tribal judges and officers who hear cases and receive the law in Deuteronomy.

stages.label: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy

quotes.quote: then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.

stages.text: Elders, judges and officers: men of middle to advanced age, mostly weathered and grey-bearded; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beards and close-cropped hair; calm, serious faces. Signature outfit: a long woven undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo cloak with a plain woven border. Carry a short wooden staff of office.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
canon.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
canon.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

canon.name: The plains of Moab
canon.note: Eastern camp across the Jordan where Moses speaks the law and dies, Deuteronomy only.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

quotes.quote: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.
in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low valley of dry grassland and scrub east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho and Beth Peor, with acacia, tamarisk and wild shrubs along the river line. Rising to the west, the bare slopes of Mount Nebo and Pisgah, with a flat-topped summit, look over the Jordan valley. Plain tents of goat hair and rough stone walls mark the Israelite encampment; no buildings of note stand in the valley.

fields.primarySubject: Veiled brilliant white-gold radiance with a fire-like glow at its heart, hanging above the summit of Horeb within a slowly moving dense cloud
fields.action: The Israelite people stand gathered at the mountain's foot, turning their faces upward toward the cloud; the radiance drifts slowly over the summit
fields.setting: Rocky slopes at the foot of Horeb, a ring of tents and camps below the mountain, open wilderness beyond under open sky
fields.secondaryElements: Faint smoke and fire-glow at the peak; cloud gathering thickly over the summit; cloaked Israelites in woven tunics and cloaks in the foreground
fields.mood: Awe, reverence and a sober weight, tinged with apprehension
fields.composition: Wide view from below the mountain, people in the lower foreground, the summit and cloud-veiled radiance occupying the upper center

conditions.place: Foot of Horeb, rocky slopes with camps below the mountain
conditions.weather: Still air, thick cloud gathering over the summit
conditions.light: Diffuse dimming daylight with the mountain's fire-glow and veiled brilliant light from the cloud
conditions.clothing: Woven tunics and cloaks for the Israelites in plain woven dress
